nodes.label: Grill-until-locked brainstorm before any plan: intent is locked task-by-task (In / Out / Needs-answer) and no plan file or code is written until the lock is approved
nodes.norm_label: grill-until-locked brainstorm before any plan

nodes.label: Intent Lock template: verbatim task table, Mermaid scope map, decisions attributed Human vs Agent-default, acceptance criteria, approval gate
nodes.norm_label: intent lock template with human vs agent-default attribution

nodes.label: A snippets.manifest.json uuid is not a snippet: the database slot must be created first with `snipset snippet add`, otherwise the snippet is absent from the app
nodes.norm_label: a manifest uuid is not a snippet slot

nodes.label: Shipped as snippet plus template only, keyword `brn`, with no new skill package, wired into snippets.manifest.json and both validators
nodes.norm_label: snippet plus template instead of a new skill package

nodes.label: The ultra plan skill goes straight to a super complete implementation plan, so intent has to be locked in a separate earlier phase for the agent to grasp it
nodes.norm_label: brainstorm separately because the plan skill skips intent locking

nodes.label: By design uuids come from the database, so the slot has to be provisioned once before the snippet can be pushed
nodes.norm_label: uuids come from the database so the slot must be provisioned

nodes.label: `DOWNLOAD_ROUTE_PLATFORMS`: each download extension resolves to exactly one platform before any lookup, case-insensitively on the last path segment, and the tag-qualified route is deliberately excluded
nodes.norm_label: download extension resolves platform before any lookup

nodes.label: The five extension routes read the platform's own channel list via T7's fetchChannelReleases instead of the repository-wide /releases/latest or an unfiltered per_page=10 scan
nodes.norm_label: channel-scoped download lookup replaces releases/latest

nodes.label: Documented second lookup stage: a bare legacy tag release is admitted only when it actually carries the file the route serves, and a namespaced other-platform release is never borrowed
nodes.norm_label: legacy bare-tag asset compatibility stage

nodes.label: Channel selection memoized 30 s per platform AND route (releaseCacheKey + cachedChannelSelection) so /exe and /msi cannot share a cache entry
nodes.norm_label: channel selection memoized per platform and route

nodes.label: T7's isWindowsInstaller does not count .msi, so an MSI-only release is absent from the Windows channel list and /msi only reaches it through the legacy stage
nodes.norm_label: isWindowsInstaller does not count msi

nodes.label: A single positional mockResolvedValueOnce was consumed by all three fetchChannelReleases pagination requests, so the versions-route test hit real fetch and returned 502
nodes.norm_label: positional fetch mock outlived pagination

nodes.label: Pre-existing fallback tests kept their assertions but their fetch fixtures became a URL-routed mock instead of a positional queue, because the GitHub call sequence changed
nodes.norm_label: url-routed fetch mock replaces positional queue

nodes.label: The known 502 had two independent causes: empty assets meant nothing matched the Windows channel, and the single positional mock was then consumed by all 3 pagination requests
nodes.norm_label: known broken test had two causes

nodes.label: A restart silently returned both allowlisted files to their HEAD state (index.js 441 lines, index.test.ts 338 lines with 9 it(), no git status entries), wiping the completed work
nodes.norm_label: restart silently restored both files to HEAD

nodes.label: The edit tool reported "Missing key: path" because the payload was too large and something was truncating it, so large replacements had to be split into smaller chunks
nodes.norm_label: edit tool payload too large drops the path key

nodes.label: Fresh RED was recorded by checking out HEAD's index.js and re-running the new test file: 6 failed / 15 passed, all assertion failures with no import or setup error
nodes.norm_label: red evidence re-verified against HEAD after the restore

nodes.label: T7's bare-tag rule is correct, so the old fixture was fixed by giving each release its real exe asset instead of weakening the rule that exposed it
nodes.norm_label: fix the fixture not the rule

nodes.label: All 775 tags in this repo are bare v* and no linux-v*/android-v* tag exists yet, so a strictly channel-scoped lookup would 404 for /deb, /appimage and /apk while only bare-tag artifacts exist
nodes.norm_label: all 775 tags are bare so strict scoping would 404

nodes.label: The earlier RED no longer described the code that would ship once the file had been restored, so it had to be re-verified cleanly against a HEAD checkout
nodes.norm_label: red evidence is stale after a silent restore

nodes.label: The memoization key includes the route as well as the platform, so /exe and /msi cannot share a single selection entry
nodes.norm_label: per-route cache key so two windows routes cannot share

nodes.label: A known extension on the tag-qualified route is deliberately not a download route because that path's own release is its authority, and the old test for it is kept as the guard
nodes.norm_label: the tag-qualified route is its own authority

nodes.label: Large edit payloads were split into several smaller chunks because the tool dropped required keys from the oversized request
nodes.norm_label: split large edits because the tool drops keys
